title_english: The Tale of the Clever Monkey and the Forest Fox
description: Classical Tai moral fable documented in Pacific Linguistics 565 (p. 392, 410), contrasting the restless impulsiveness of the monkey with the patient cunning of the forest fox, illustrating that thoughtful reflection surpasses hurried pride.

full_translation: A agile monkey lived high among the leafy canopy of a great forest tree. A sly forest fox came wandering beneath the shady branches looking for food. The monkey peered down and chattered: 'Friend Fox, what do you seek along the damp ground?' The fox looked up slyly: 'I am searching for the sweet ripe figs that fall from the canopy.' The impetuous monkey leapt down onto a low branch to offer fruit to the fox. Instantly the deceitful fox snapped its jaws, seizing the monkey's foot in a firm grip. Using quick wit, the monkey laughed: 'Foolish fox! You have bitten a rotten bamboo root, not my leg!' Deceived by the monkey's laughter, the fox let go, and the monkey sprang safely back into the high tree. He who maintains mindfulness and composure triumphs over the most perilous snares.
title: The Tale of the Clever Monkey and the Forest Fox
